column15: Independent bottler founded 1895, Elgin. Speymalt is their dedicated range name for Macallan-sourced whisky (see speymalt row). Bottler has no single house peat level.
30-35ppm; medium/gentler peat by Islay standards per multiple sources, less brash than Ardbeg/Lagavulin. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples.
Oldest continuously operating distillery in Scotland; malt predominantly unpeated. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples; also the heart of the Chivas Regal blend.
Unpeated malted barley to tightly defined maltster specs. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples (Speymalt range).
'Beast of Dufftown' -- meaty/sulphury house character, not peat. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples.
Unpeated or very lightly peated barley; sherry-cask-forward house style. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples.
Unusual peated Highland malt (most Highland distilleries are unpeated), 12-14ppm; historically the smoky backbone of Teacher's blend. Named in Gordon & MacPhail samples.
Gordon & MacPhail's dedicated range name reserved for independently-bottled Macallan; spirit is distilled at Macallan so peat profile is identical (none), not merely inherited.

Strathisla-led premium blend. Sources describe a subtle/elegant smokiness from cask finishing rather than heavy peating -- classified light rather than none out of caution; genuinely uncertain, hence low confidence. A separate 'Extra Smooth & Smoky' cask-finish SKU exists but no rule was written for it (finish-derived, not confirmed peat).

Irish blend (pot still + malt + grain); William Grant & Sons since 2010, new Tullamore distillery opened 2014. defaultTypeName left empty: the wider range also includes single malt and single pot still expressions beyond the flagship blend.

Hombo Shuzo operates TWO distilleries (Shinshu, Nagano + Tsunuki, Kagoshima) under the Mars brand; Shinshu alone runs FOUR peating levels (unpeated / 3.5ppm / 20ppm / 50ppm) depending on release, so no single peat profile applies -- left unknown deliberately. Samples span both distilleries and several product lines (Iwai, Kasei, Cosmo, Tsunuki, Y.A).

column7: Edradour Distillery Company (Signatory Vintage / Andrew Symington)
column15: Core Edradour range is unpeated. The distillery also produces the heavily-peated Ballechin line since 2003 (separate producer row, sibling brand -- do not average).
~55ppm heavily peated; produced at Edradour distillery since 2003, first release 2006. Sibling of unpeated Edradour, same distillery.
Air-dried, unpeated barley ('no peat is used, differentiating Tamdhu from Highland Park'); sherry-cask-only maturation is the house signature.
Blend of 41 Highland/Speyside malt+grain whiskies, triple-matured with an ex-sherry-cask marrying stage; no peat character reported. Input brand string 'Whyte Mackay' is missing the ampersand.
100% Kentucky straight rye whiskey; wine-cask-finished expressions (Margaux/Pauillac/Sauternes Barriques) plus a Barrel Proof base release. Rye whiskey, no peat used.
Also referred to as Thompson's Kentucky Artisan Distillery, Crestwood, KY; pre-Prohibition-era all-copper pot still. Source of Coalition's rye. American rye whiskey, no peat.
Distilled from unpeated barley grain; historically a blending malt, bottled as vintage releases since 2007.

Malt/grain sourced from Canada and Scotland, aged/blended/bottled in Japan inside a disused railway tunnel near Hiroshima. Base range (standard/Kiwami/Premium) is not peated -- see rule.tsv for the separate 'Togouchi Peated' line.

column7: Grace O'Malley Spirits (Inis Tine Uisce Teoranta)
column15: Whiskey brand with no own distillery yet (one is under construction); sourced mainly from Great Northern Distillery and other suppliers, blended/finished at Good Spirits Bottling, Dundalk. No peat reported. defaultTypeName left empty: portfolio spans blends and single malt releases.

Kentucky straight bourbon distillery (Versailles, KY); standard corn/rye/malted-barley mashbill, no peated malt used -- peat is not part of American whiskey tradition. defaultTypeName left empty: the brand also releases Woodford Reserve Rye alongside the bourbon range, even though none of this batch's 6 samples name it.

Independent bottler, Glasgow, est. 1948. Owns Scallywag (Speyside blended malt) and The Gauldrons (Campbeltown blended malt) ranges among others (not added as separate rows: no direct peat citation found for either). Hunter Laing & Co split off in 2013 -- Old Malt Cask is covered separately under that lineage (see old-malt-cask row). Input brand string 'Douglas Laingcompany' is a mangled/concatenated spelling of 'Douglas Laing & Company', matching the sample 'Douglas Laing&Company Jura Vintage 1995'.

Post-2018 core range (10/12/18, Seven Wood, Journey) uses unpeated or very lightly peated malt with a small proportion of peated spirit vatted in ('subtly smoky'); occasional heavily-peated limited runs exist (Prophecy). Older/independently-bottled vintages named in samples ('Jura Vintage 1995', 'Old Malt Cask Jura') may predate the 2018 convention and could differ -- treat single-cask releases with caution. Named in both Douglas Laing and Old Malt Cask samples.

Hunter Laing & Co's flagship single-cask range, spanning many distilleries (Wikipedia confirms the 2013 Douglas Laing/Hunter Laing split; Hunter Laing's own Scarabus listing confirms the company bottles single malt independently). Modeled as kind=bottler since the range spans many distilleries with no single house peat level. Scarabus (separate row) is also a Hunter Laing product; bottlerSlug=old-malt-cask stands in for the parent company to avoid inventing an extra 'hunter-laing' row.
Unpeated malt; core component of the Bell's blend. Named in Old Malt Cask samples.
Unpeated malt, triple-distilled -- signature Lowland style. Named in Old Malt Cask samples.

Speyside distillery (formerly Braes of Glenlivet), mostly a blending component for Chivas Brothers. No direct peat citation found (not opened), left unknown rather than assumed unpeated. Named in Old Malt Cask samples ('Braeval 1997 The Old Malt Cask').

Speyside distillery, principal component of the Ballantine's blend. No direct peat citation found (not opened), left unknown rather than assumed unpeated. Named in Old Malt Cask samples ('Miltonduff 1995 The Old Malt Cask').

Crolly Distillery, County Donegal -- first licensed whiskey distillery in Donegal since the 1840s. Tasting notes show no smoke/peat character (vanilla, caramel, orchard fruit, oak). 'Croithlí' is the Irish-language place name spelled with a fada; catalogue brand string 'Croithli' drops it.

Budget blended Scotch trademark, originally J. MacArthur & Co (1877); now part of International Beverage Holdings (Inver House group, also owns Old Pulteney/anCnoc/Speyburn/Balblair). No peat character reported.

Single malt from an undisclosed Islay distillery ('mystery malt'), launched by Hunter Laing for Feis Ile 2019, tied to the opening of their own Ardnahoe distillery. Official notes cite 'Islay peat smoke' aroma; exact ppm/intensity not published, so classified medium rather than heavy out of caution. Source distillery deliberately left blank per the undisclosed-label rule (rule 3).
'Pact' series -- master distiller John Rempe combines sourced/aged bourbons into limited annual vattings (a true blend, no single distillery of origin). Kentucky straight bourbon, no peat.

French single malt launched 2019 by Whiskies Du Monde, made exclusively from French raw materials, non-chill-filtered. Base range unpeated -- see rule.tsv for the separate Peated expression. Correct accented spelling is 'Evade' (with acute accent on the final e); catalogue brand string 'Evade' is the unaccented form.
Own-label American-style whiskey, no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule (3 near-identical sample names, name evokes Jack Daniel's).

Curated range of undisclosed single malts from various Islay distilleries (Elixir Distillers keeps sources confidential; enthusiasts widely link some batches to Caol Ila/Laphroaig/Bunnahabhain, none officially confirmed). Every release is marketed around Islay's 'smoky, maritime character', so peat is recorded as heavy despite the source distillery being left blank per the undisclosed-label rule.
London-based independent bottler, launched Port Askaig in 2009; also releases the Elements of Islay range. Non-chill-filtered, no added colour across releases.

Umbrella brand spanning THREE Diageo distilleries marketed regionally -- Glen Ord (Highland), Glendullan (Speyside) and Dufftown (Speyside); no single parentSlug applies, left empty. All three are conventional fruity/nutty unpeated malts, so peat is confidently none regardless of which one a given bottling is. region/legalRegion left empty since it spans Highland and Speyside.

Lightest-bodied of the Jim Beam small-batch bourbon family, high-rye mashbill. defaultTypeName left empty: the line also includes a Dark Rye expression alongside the bourbon. parentSlug=jim-beam expected to be seeded by another batch (globally known Beam Suntory distillery/brand) -- not created here.

Blended malt Scotch vatting eight Speyside single malts, created for the Craigellachie Hotel's Copper Dog pub by Piers Adam and master blender Stuart Morrison. Fruity/honeyed profile (honey, toast, pecan, apple, fudge, orange peel), no smoke reported.

Moldovan whisky ('Scottish technology'), 3-year-old barley malt; cinnamon/vanilla/stone-fruit profile, no smoke reported. Sold mainly in Ukrainian/Eastern European retail (also listed on rozetka.com.ua and maudau.com.ua).
Own-label American-style whiskey ('Straight Old Reserve'), no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule.
Own-label blended Scotch, no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule. Input brand string 'Matt D Arcy' has no apostrophe; samples spell it 'Matt D'Arcy'.

Vertically integrated single malt distillery in Rozelieures, Lorraine (own barley, malting, distilling, maturation); founded early 2000s, first release 2007. Base/Origine range unpeated -- see rule.tsv for the separate Tourbe (peated) line.
Blended Scotch whisky, limited information available; 5- and 12-year expressions listed on Whiskybase. No peat/smoke character found in available sources, hence low confidence despite the citation.

Re-opened 2014, first single malt distillery in Glasgow for 100+ years; name references the city's original 1770 distilling licence. Signature Range = The Original (unpeated) + Triple Distilled (unpeated) + The Peated -- see rule.tsv for the peated expression. Sample product '1770 The Original' is the unpeated flagship. Catalogue brand string is the bare number '1770'.
Own-label / limited bottling ('Thunder in the Glens Anniversary'), no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule.
Own-label blended Scotch, no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule.

Flagship consumer brand of Fuji Gotemba Distillery (foot of Mt Fuji, Shizuoka), launched 2020; range spans Single Grain/Single Malt/Single Blended, defaultTypeName left empty accordingly. No peat mentioned in any source; the distillery is not known for peated production.
Lowland single grain, launched 2014 (Diageo / David Beckham / Simon Fuller). 'Clubman' (named in samples) is the more affordable 2016 variant. Grain whisky, no peat.
Largest grain distillery in Scotland, wholly owned by Diageo since 1997; founded by John Haig 1824. Source distillery of Haig Club.

American blended whiskey (70% 7-year corn whiskey, 30% young rye) from Two James Spirits, Detroit. Smoke comes from a proprietary Asian-tea maceration process, NOT peated malt -- non-peat smoky tag recorded in flavor.tsv, analogous to Jack Daniel's charcoal mellowing.
Own-label, no web presence found (name likely evokes the cocktail); fast-tracked per own-label rule.

Sherry-cask blended malt from The Macallan, Highland Park, Glenturret and Glenrothes; rebranded 'Naked Malt' in 2018. One constituent (Highland Park) is medium-peated, but the finished blend's own tasting notes describe rich/fruity sherry character with no smoke, so recorded as none. Ownership was Edrington; ownership of the sibling Famous Grouse brand moved to William Grant & Sons in 2024/2025 (see famous-grouse) -- left owner empty here since Naked Malt's own sale was not separately confirmed.

Blended Scotch (min. 25% malt content) evoking the historic Tullymet distillery (built 1812 as Auchnagie, renamed Tullymet 1890, long since closed) -- heritage branding, not a claim that the liquid comes from that site. No peat/smoke mentioned; described as smooth and elegant.
Irish whiskey (triple-distilled grain + double-distilled malt blend), aged 10 years in ex-bourbon casks, bottled for the German band Rammstein. No peat reported (standard Irish blend style).

'Shenk's Homestead' is a Michter's Kentucky Straight Sour Mash Whiskey bottling; defaultTypeName left empty since sour mash whiskey is not one of the closed category values. American whiskey, no peat. parentSlug=michters expected to be seeded by another batch (well-known US heritage distillery brand) -- not created here.

Best-selling Scotch blend in Scotland; sherry/toffee/honey house style, standard range is not peated ('relatively mild in terms of smoke'). Ownership transitioned from Edrington to William Grant & Sons (sale announced Sept 2024, UK CMA clearance March 2025) -- owner recorded as the post-transition company. See rule.tsv for the separate Smoky Black expression.

'Ocean-fused' blended whisky using malt from coastal Japanese distilleries plus grain whisky, matured in pine barrels; Osaka-based Yoshino Spirits/Kamiki Shuzo. 'Godzilla' edition (in samples) is a 70th-anniversary collaboration with Toho Co. No peat/smoke reported in tasting descriptions, hence still only low confidence.
